channel.title: Medics Musings: Health Care News of the Day
channel.description: One real health care story a day, with a satirical headline and take from two doctors.

item.title: Utah Streamlines Prescribing by Removing Step Where Anyone Reviews Anything First
item.description: Prior authorization will presumably still require a human, ideally one on hold. Still, it's inspiring to watch regulators innovate on the single step of care involving a licensed clinician, rather than the dozens involving a fax machine. The sandbox is real. The accountability remains in a pilot phase. The real story: Utah plows ahead with more health AI pilots for prescriptions, women’s health (STAT) https://www.statnews.com/2026/10/05/utah-expands-health-ai-sandbox-picks-third-party-auditors/

item.title: Experts Announce October Has Arrived Again, Urge Flu Shots Before the Flu
item.description: Flu season returns annually with the reliability of a deductible reset, and the public health message is sound: get vaccinated early. The harder part is the system around it, with its pharmacy portals, coverage questions and a fall respiratory menu that needs a navigator. Influenza is predictable. Our logistics somehow aren't. The real story: Why Now Is an Ideal Time for Flu Protection (MedPage Today) https://www.medpagetoday.com/infectiousdisease/vaccines/123250

item.title: Governors Request Extension on Assignment Requiring Others to Submit Paperwork on Time
item.description: States have asked HHS for more time to implement Medicaid work requirements. Nothing signals confidence in a verification system like the administrators needing a deadline extension to build it. We trust the same flexibility will be offered to everyone who has to navigate it. The real story: Governors ask HHS for more time to implement Medicaid work requirements (Healthcare Dive) https://www.healthcaredive.com/news/medicaid-work-requirements-governors-ask-hhs-delay-letter/831992/

item.title: Insurers Say Billing AI Will Raise Costs; Billing Companies Say It Won't
item.description: Insurers say AI will drive health costs up. The companies selling AI billing tools say it will drive costs down. Both have a financial stake in being right, and neither number comes with a citation. The physician who has to document the visit either way was not asked. The real story: Insurers say AI could add billions in health costs. Billing companies disagree (Healthcare Dive) https://www.healthcaredive.com/news/insurers-say-ai-could-add-billions-in-health-costs-billing-companies-disag/831497/

item.title: Insurers Discover Generosity Was Never in the Business Plan
item.description: Every fall, Medicare Advantage plans trim a benefit or two and call it right-sizing. The pattern holds again for 2027: fewer extras, same premiums, and an insurer newsletter next spring wondering why satisfaction scores dropped. The real story: Here’s how much insurers are cutting Medicare Advantage plans for 2027 (Healthcare Dive) https://www.healthcaredive.com/news/medicare-advantage-cuts-2027-cms-landscape/831563/

item.title: Pharma Stunned to Learn Patents Were Supposed to Expire
item.description: Evergreening, for the uninitiated, is the art of changing a drug’s coating, dose or delivery just enough to reset the patent clock. An Indonesian court just said no to it. It remains the only corner of medicine where the old treatment keeps getting newer and the price never gets lower. The real story: Indonesian ruling against ‘patent evergreening’ by pharma industry sends critical message, patient advocates say (STAT) https://www.statnews.com/pharmalot/2026/09/24/indonesian-court-rules-against-patent-evergreening-boosting-access-medicines/
